passages.text: Gather yourselves, gather together, O shameful nation, before the decree takes effect and the day passes like chaff, before the burning anger of the LORD comes upon you, before the Day of the LORD’s anger comes upon you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to a nation that has brought shame upon itself.
He commands this nation to gather together.
He tells them to come together quickly.
He warns them to do this before His decree takes effect.
He warns them to act before the day passes away like chaff blown by the wind.
He tells them to gather before the LORD’s burning anger comes upon them.
He warns them to act before the Day of the LORD’s anger arrives.
passages.original: הִֽתְקוֹשְׁשׁ֖וּ וָק֑וֹשּׁוּ הַגּ֖וֹי לֹ֥א נִכְסָֽף׃ בְּטֶ֙רֶם֙ לֶ֣דֶת חֹ֔ק כְּמֹ֖ץ עָ֣בַר י֑וֹם בְּטֶ֣רֶם׀ לֹא־ יָב֣וֹא עֲלֵיכֶ֗ם חֲרוֹן֙ אַף־ יְהוָ֔ה בְּטֶ֙רֶם֙ לֹא־ יָב֣וֹא עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם י֖וֹם אַף־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Seek the LORD, all you humble of the earth who carry out His justice. Seek righteousness; seek humility. Perhaps you will be sheltered on the day of the LORD’s anger.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
He is just.
He will bring a day of anger.
You are humble people on the earth.
You do what is right.
You follow God’s justice.
Seek the LORD.
Seek what is right.
Seek to be humble.
Maybe God will hide you.
Maybe He will protect you on the day of His anger.
passages.original: בַּקְּשׁ֤וּ אֶת־ יְהוָה֙ כָּל־ עַנְוֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִשְׁפָּט֖וֹ פָּעָ֑לוּ בַּקְּשׁוּ־ צֶ֙דֶק֙ בַּקְּשׁ֣וּ עֲנָוָ֔ה אוּלַי֙ תִּסָּ֣תְר֔וּ בְּי֖וֹם אַף־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: For Gaza will be abandoned, and Ashkelon left in ruins. Ashdod will be driven out at noon, and Ekron will be uprooted.
passages.sermon:
Gaza is a city.
Gaza will be abandoned.
Ashkelon is a city.
Ashkelon will become ruins.
Ashdod is a city.
People will drive out Ashdod at noon.
Ekron is a city.
People will uproot Ekron.
passages.original: כִּ֤י עַזָּה֙ עֲזוּבָ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ה וְאַשְׁקְל֖וֹן לִשְׁמָמָ֑ה אַשְׁדּ֗וֹד בַּֽצָּהֳרַ֙יִם֙ יְגָ֣רְשׁ֔וּהָ וְעֶקְר֖וֹן תֵּעָקֵֽר׃ס

passages.text: Woe to the dwellers of the seacoast, O nation of the Cherethites! The word of the LORD is against you, O Canaan, land of the Philistines: “I will destroy you, and no one will be left.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people who live by the sea.
These people are called the Cherethites.
The LORD’s word is against you, Cherethites.
You live in Canaan, the land of the Philistines.
The LORD says, “I will destroy you.”
No one will remain living there.
passages.original: ה֗וֹי יֹֽשְׁבֵ֛י חֶ֥בֶל הַיָּ֖ם גּ֣וֹי כְּרֵתִ֑ים דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֣ה עֲלֵיכֶ֗ם כְּנַ֙עַן֙ אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֖יךְ מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃

passages.text: So the seacoast will become a land of pastures, with wells for shepherds and folds for sheep.
passages.sermon:
The seacoast will change.
It will become a land of pastures.
Shepherds will live there.
There will be wells for the shepherds.
There will be folds for sheep.
passages.original: וְֽהָיְתָ֞ה חֶ֣בֶל הַיָּ֗ם נְוֺ֛ת כְּרֹ֥ת רֹעִ֖ים וְגִדְר֥וֹת צֹֽאן׃

passages.text: The coast will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; there they will find pasture. They will lie down in the evening among the houses of Ashkelon, for the LORD their God will attend to them and restore their captives.
passages.sermon:
The remnant of the house of Judah will own the coast.
They will find pasture there.
They will rest in the evening among the houses of Ashkelon.
The LORD is their God.
The LORD will care for them.
The LORD will restore their captives.
passages.original: וְהָ֣יָה חֶ֗בֶל לִשְׁאֵרִ֛ית בֵּ֥ית יְהוּדָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם יִרְע֑וּן בְּבָתֵּ֣י אַשְׁקְל֗וֹן בָּעֶ֙רֶב֙ יִרְבָּצ֔וּן כִּ֧י יִפְקְדֵ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם וְשָׁ֥ב שְׁבוּתָם׃

passages.text: “I have heard the reproach of Moab and the insults of the Ammonites, who have taunted My people and threatened their borders.
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God says, “I have heard the reproach of Moab.
I have heard the insults of the Ammonites.
Moab and Ammon have taunted My people.
They have threatened the borders of My people.”
passages.original: שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ חֶרְפַּ֣ת מוֹאָ֔ב וְגִדּוּפֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן אֲשֶׁ֤ר חֵֽרְפוּ֙ אֶת־ עַמִּ֔י וַיַּגְדִּ֖ילוּ עַל־ גְּבוּלָֽם׃

passages.text: Therefore, as surely as I live,” declares the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, “surely Moab will be like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah— a place of weeds and salt pits, a perpetual wasteland. The remnant of My people will plunder them; the remainder of My nation will dispossess them.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the God of Israel.
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
The LORD of Hosts lives forever.
The LORD of Hosts makes a promise.
Moab will become like Sodom.
The Ammonites will become like Gomorrah.
Their land will be covered with weeds.
Their land will have salt pits.
Their land will become a wasteland forever.
The remnant of God's people will plunder Moab and Ammon.
The rest of God's nation will take their land.
passages.original: לָכֵ֣ן חַי־ אָ֡נִי נְאֻם֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כִּֽי־ מוֹאָ֞ב כִּסְדֹ֤ם תִּֽהְיֶה֙ וּבְנֵ֤י עַמּוֹן֙ כַּֽעֲמֹרָ֔ה מִמְשַׁ֥ק חָר֛וּל וּמִכְרֵה־ מֶ֥לַח וּשְׁמָמָ֖ה עַד־ עוֹלָ֑ם שְׁאֵרִ֤ית עַמִּי֙ יְבָזּ֔וּם וְיֶ֥תֶר גּוֹי יִנְחָלֽוּם׃

passages.text: This they shall have in return for their pride, for taunting and mocking the people of the LORD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is God over all.
Some people acted with pride.
They taunted the LORD’s people.
They mocked the LORD’s people.
God will give them a punishment.
This punishment is because of their pride.
This punishment is because they taunted and mocked God’s people.
passages.original: זֹ֥את לָהֶ֖ם תַּ֣חַת גְּאוֹנָ֑ם כִּ֤י חֵֽרְפוּ֙ וַיַּגְדִּ֔לוּ עַל־ עַ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: The LORD will be terrifying to them when He starves all the gods of the earth. Then the nations of every shore will bow in worship to Him, each in its own place.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD is powerful and holy.
The LORD will act against the nations.
The LORD will be terrifying to the nations.
The LORD will destroy all the gods of the earth.
No false god will remain.
People from every nation will see this.
People from every shore will bow down to the LORD.
Each person will worship the LORD in his own place.
passages.original: נוֹרָ֤א יְהוָה֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כִּ֣י רָזָ֔ה אֵ֖ת כָּל־ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיִשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ־ לוֹ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִמְּקוֹמ֔וֹ כֹּ֖ל אִיֵּ֥י הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

passages.text: “You too, O Cushites, will be slain by My sword.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the Cushites.
The LORD is powerful and judges nations.
The LORD says to the Cushites, “You also will fall by My sword.”
The LORD will strike down the Cushites with His sword.
The Cushites will be killed by the LORD’s power.
passages.original: גַּם־ אַתֶּ֣ם כּוּשִׁ֔ים חַֽלְלֵ֥י חַרְבִּ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃

passages.text: And He will stretch out His hand against the north and destroy Assyria; He will make Nineveh a desolation, as dry as a desert.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is powerful and judges nations.
He will stretch out His hand against the north.
He will destroy Assyria.
He will make Nineveh a desolation.
Nineveh will become as dry as a desert.
passages.original: וְיֵ֤ט יָדוֹ֙ עַל־ צָפ֔וֹן וִֽיאַבֵּ֖ד אֶת־ אַשּׁ֑וּר וְיָשֵׂ֤ם אֶת־ נִֽינְוֵה֙ לִשְׁמָמָ֔ה צִיָּ֖ה כַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

passages.text: Herds will lie down in her midst, creatures of every kind. Both the desert owl and screech owl will roost atop her pillars. Their calls will sound from the window, but desolation will lie on the threshold, for He will expose the beams of cedar.
passages.sermon:
God will destroy Nineveh.
Herds will lie down in the middle of the city.
Every kind of wild animal will be there.
The desert owl will rest on her pillars.
The screech owl will also rest there.
Their calls will come from the windows.
Desolation will cover the threshold.
God will strip the cedar beams bare.
passages.original: וְרָבְצ֨וּ בְתוֹכָ֤הּ עֲדָרִים֙ כָּל־ חַיְתוֹ־ ג֔וֹי גַּם־ קָאַת֙ גַּם־ קִפֹּ֔ד בְּכַפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ יָלִ֑ינוּ ק֠וֹל יְשׁוֹרֵ֤ר בַּֽחַלּוֹן֙ חֹ֣רֶב בַּסַּ֔ף כִּ֥י אַרְזָ֖ה עֵרָֽה׃

passages.text: This carefree city that dwells securely, that thinks to herself: “I am it, and there is none besides me,” what a ruin she has become, a resting place for beasts. Everyone who passes by her hisses and shakes his fist.
passages.sermon:
This city was once joyful.
She lived in safety.
She felt secure.
She said in her heart, “I am all that matters.
No one else is like me.”
Now she has become a ruin.
Wild animals rest there.
Everyone who passes by her hisses.
They shake their fists at her.
passages.original: זֹ֠את הָעִ֤יר הָעַלִּיזָה֙ הַיּוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת לָבֶ֔טַח הָאֹֽמְרָה֙ בִּלְבָבָ֔הּ אֲנִ֖י וְאַפְסִ֣י ע֑וֹד אֵ֣יךְ׀ הָיְתָ֣ה לְשַׁמָּ֗ה מַרְבֵּץ֙ לַֽחַיָּ֔ה כֹּ֚ל עוֹבֵ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ יִשְׁרֹ֖ק יָנִ֥יעַ יָדֽוֹ׃ס
